correctness.rationale: The adjacency quadratic relation gives three orthogonal eigenspaces. Primitivity forces strict two-point correlations in both nonprincipal projectors, hence Gram rank two in each and one in the principal eigenspace: bright rank five. Positive rates rule out nondecaying bright eigenmodes, so capture is exactly the bright projection. Its diagonal yields the explicit 2x2-inverse site law, and adjacency counts give all populations. Independent SVD projector checks cover 598 sink pairs and 8849 sites across seven graphs; exact arithmetic examples check formulas. An imprimitive counterexample validates necessity of the boundary; no finite test replaces the proof.

value.rationale: Uniform single-sink transport has dimension three in primitive strongly regular graphs; two sinks universally give five independent channels and a full exact site-resolved law, including non-vertex-transitive and nonisomorphic pairs with identical parameters. The parameter-only indistinguishability, class-size classification and sharp imprimitive boundary are motivated network benchmarks rather than an arbitrary table, with a concrete use for interpreting quantum loss experiments and graph discrimination.
